ev.q: During 2008–2016, the annual number of diagnoses of HIV infection increased 3% per year among MSM aged 13–29 years
During this period, the annual number of diagnoses increased among MSM aged 13–29 years (APC = 2.9).
the number of MSM aged 13–29 years living with HIV increased in 42 jurisdictions
younger black/African American MSM who accounted for 49% of all diagnoses
Among 236,150 MSM with HIV infection diagnosed during 2008–2016, a total of 106,258 (45%) were aged 13–29 years
The number of HIV diagnoses among MSM aged 13–29 years was four times that of MSM aged ≥50 years.
During this period, the annual number of diagnoses increased among MSM aged 13–29 years (APC = 2.9).
All states and U.S. dependent areas report cases of HIV infection and associated patient demographic and clinical information to NHSS.

methods_quotes.q: Trends in annual diagnoses of HIV infection among MSM during 2008–2016 were measured using estimated annual percent change (APC)
The APC is calculated by using a generalized log linear model.
Changes were considered statistically significant if the APC’s 95% confidence interval (CI) excluded zero.
Data statistically adjusted to account for missing transmission category.
